title: Squirrel-Kastella
text: “Even so, Tiger Girl won’t back down, I’d wager.”

The depth of Tiger Girl’s love was truly admirable, I say. I too must go on thinking of Filo-tan endlessly like that, no matter what. In every world except the first one, though, she’s been rather demure, and whenever I approach, she just gets scared off, muttering about whirlwinds of love.
“Was she like, weirdly pushy? That Atla-chan from the first world?”
“Indeed. No matter how far you tried to push her away, she pursued with an obsession that knew no bounds.”

That kind of aggressive persistence always reminds me of a lovesick pig, so honestly, I’m a bit weak to it, I say. Still, Tiger Girl had a certain manliness to her that set her apart from a lovesick pig, so I do understand the difference.
“It’s a relief that Atla-san in this world is so mild-mannered.”
“Yeah. Apparently Fohl-kun got called in to stop Atla-chan’s rampage… but can he actually stop her?”
“Apparently Tiger Girl finds Tiger Guy a nuisance and treats him rather coldly, but since she can’t completely get rid of him, he’s useful as a way to slow her down, I say.”
“Well, Fohl-kun and Atla-chan are a close brother-sister pair after all. Fohl-kun’s a total sister-complex case, but he’s apparently supported her admirably all this time.”
“According to the Filolial-samas, Tiger Guy has apparently confessed his feelings to Father before, I say.”
“Wait, hold on, isn’t there something seriously wrong with that premise?”
Father demanded a stop right there.
“I think I sort of understand that, though. Fohl-san did carry you off when you were turned into a Peckle, after all.”
“It’s not out of the question that he was trying to get the siblings fighting over Naofumi-san, so he could maintain his life with Raphtalia-san in the meantime.”
“That’s kind of a villain move… but if he keeps butting in no matter how much you refuse him, I guess calling him in makes sense.”
Ren and Itsuki nodded along in agreement while eating.
“That’s awful… well, this world’s Fohl-kun doesn’t show any signs of that, so let’s just be glad.”
“Who knows, though? He might come at you insisting he can’t forget Peckle-Naofumi.”
“If you’re gonna say that, then what about you and Luna-chan, Ren? Even if you turned back to your original form, she’d still remember you, so it’d be the same thing.”
“Ugh…”
Ren had dug his own grave, I say. Though personally, I think it would make Luna-chan happier if Ren just stayed as Inult.
“…Let’s drop this topic. Itsuki?”
“Why are you tossing this to me?”
“If you keep poking at it, I’ll steer the conversation straight into something that’ll make you squirm, no matter what.”
“You don’t have to threaten me like that.”
“Anyway, getting back to it—Fohl-kun went to my world, and it sounds like he enjoyed himself decently.”
“Indeed. As souvenir talk, he told all sorts of stories about Father’s world, I say.”
I could recall this well.
“What I’m curious about is whether it was the cooking manga world or not. Did the first-world me or Ren-san ever ask him about it?”
“Regrettably, I never heard, I say.”
At the very least, no one had asked Tiger Guy in front of me. Though it’s possible they did while I was out somewhere.
“Argh… why didn’t I ask?! Me, of all people!”
“Yeah! Why didn’t I ask either!? That should’ve been the first thing on my mind.”
“Well, that world’s Ren has all sorts of psychological growth and shadows, and Itsuki seems to have gone through something too… so maybe they’re just different from how you two are now?”
“It does feel rare to see the two of you like this, I admit.”

Both Ren and Itsuki in the first world had been fairly quiet types. Ren, in fact, had been desperately courting Éclair and Assistant. Itsuki had been calmly carrying out his duties alongside Riska. They’d seemed to get along well enough, though. In other worlds… well, Ren aside, it was rare to see Itsuki this lively.
“And yet that’s the one thing I’m curious about regarding Naofumi-san’s world… it’s the only real clue we have.”
“Thinking about it that way, the reason you want to visit Naofumi’s world comes down to food.”

“Oh come on… even if my world really were the cooking manga world, wouldn’t that just make it even more mundane? You can already do cooking battles in Zeltoble, so this world should be plenty, right?”
“Well… I have no objections to raise regarding Naofumi-san’s cooking skills. Even if it were true, I doubt I could adapt to that world anyway.”
“Out of all of us, Itsuki’s the only one who doesn’t cook—doesn’t it occur to you to maybe learn?”

That was certainly true. When it came to cooking, Father stood at the top, and I followed close behind, I say. Ren? Without Father’s kitchen knife, I have no intention of losing to him. As for Itsuki, he was the one who stayed away from cooking-related matters. All he ever did was help out wearing the apron Rafuemon gave him.
“I’m more of an eater, so that’s fine by me.”
“Sigh…”
“More importantly, make dessert too, Naofumi-san.”
“I’m impressed you’re demanding dessert of all things in a place like this. If I made udon, you’d probably ask for tempura next.”
“That’s actually a solid suggestion. So, what will dessert be, I wonder?”
Father’s sweets, made under these very conditions—now that was something, I say.
“Sweets, huh… hmm. Well, we do have flour as a drop item, at least…”
And so Father looked around at his surroundings… then fixed his gaze on Itsuki’s face.
“W-what?”
“Alright.”

With that, Father took out the flour, kneaded it with water, rolled it into balls, skewered them on sticks, brushed them with oil, and had me heat them with magic. I thought it might be donuts, but they stayed round, and I figured it must be some variant of the Okinawan sweet sāta andagī—except only half of each sphere got a proper browning.
“And the finishing touch, Motoyasu-kun. Could you use fire magic to cook them through without burning them?”
“Leave it to me, I say.”

And so, several half-golden, beautifully browned… suzu-kasutera—bell-shaped castella—came into being. Since it was a makeshift effort, only the general shape had been arranged; Father remarked he’d have liked to use a proper mold. Apparently a takoyaki griddle would have been ideal. He dusted the suzu-kasutera with sugar and held them out to Itsuki.
“Here. Made these sweets by your request, Itsuki. Suzu-kasutera.”
“I see.”
Ren, looking satisfied, popped one of the suzu-kasutera into his mouth.
“What do you mean, ‘I see’!? Why suzu-kasutera of all things, here of all places!?”
Father looked away. Allow me to add eyes and a handle to the suzu-kasutera with caramel and hand it over to Itsuki.
“Ah, I see how it is.”
Ren swiftly transformed his sword into Father’s beloved kitchen knife and carved the edges into the shape of ears.
“Precisely so, I say.”
Yes—for Itsuki the squirrel, a squirrel-faced suzu-kasutera, presented as a gift, I say.
“Itsuki-kasutera, I say.”
“Don’t flaunt something you already knew so shamelessly! What is this teamwork!? Please stop damaging my reputation like this!”
More importantly! Itsuki went on, quite the chatterbox.
“Naofumi-san. I demand a full explanation for why you chose suzu-kasutera.”
“Uh… I dunno, just looked around and it kind of came to me?”

“You just modeled my head after a suzu-kasutera, didn’t you!? If you top this with a chocolate command-module shaped like that famous lunar lander number eleven, you’re going to call it ‘Squirrel-Kastella,’ aren’t you!?”
“Itsuki-kasutera works fine as a name. Looks like Cal Mira Island has a new local specialty.”
“Why not just go simple and call it Squirrel-Kastella?”
“Who told either of you to come up with a clever name!? I don’t want that kind of local specialty! And Naofumi-san, don’t you dare play dumb either!”
I wondered what kind of response the first-world Father would have given here. Somehow, I felt he’d have said it plainly.
“Obviously because your head looked like a suzu-kasutera to me, that’s why.”

That’s the sort of thing he’d probably have said. After all, on occasions like Valentine’s Day, he used to make surprisingly elaborate sugar-craft figurines. Once, he even made a giant cookie modeled after a Filolial-sama—no wait, not just a cookie, sablés too. He’d developed them commercially as Filolial Sablés and sold them. For some reason, he’d always given the extras to me most of the time.
“Naofumi-san! I demand sweets modeled after everyone here!”
Itsuki banged on the table repeatedly in protest. Was he a child or something?
“You’re asking for that here, of all places…? I don’t exactly have the leisure to whip up novelty local-specialty goods right now.”
“I have no obligation to take instructions from people who just slapped together some suzu-kasutera and shaped it to look like my head!”

Itsuki spun the skewered suzu-kasutera around and around in protest—a rather memorable sight, I say. In the end, we managed to placate him by promising to make something once we’d finished clearing the dungeon, and so we pressed onward.
